name: Open flavour and off-flavour profiles of Vietnam's farmed fish
what: A public dataset of the odour-active and taste compounds of cooked tra catfish (pangasius), tilapia, carp and pond loach, with the main off-flavours (for example geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol), measured by gas chromatography with mass spectrometry and with olfactometry (GC-MS and GC-O) and linked to a trained sensory panel. Published openly for makers of plant-based, fermented, hybrid or cultivated seafood
why_vietnam: Vietnam is the world's main pangasius producer and farms tilapia, carp and pond loach at scale, so reference fish of known origin and feed are easy to sample. Vietnamese groups already run sensory work on pangasius flavour and study off-flavour in pond tilapia. Coefficient Giving's 2026 call names exactly these species as a priority and funds open, pre-competitive flavour data. No play or public good in the study covers flavour
must_be_true: A Vietnamese laboratory with GC-MS and access to GC-O (in Vietnam or through a partner abroad); a trained descriptive panel; an international co-applicant; a funder round open to Vietnamese teams (Coefficient Giving in 2027 or similar); agreement to publish the data openly
kill_tests: No Coefficient Giving or comparable round open to Vietnamese teams by the end of 2027; no Vietnamese laboratory can run or reach GC-O; a funded team abroad publishes the same profiles first (then Vietnam uses them and stops)
first_customers: Makers of plant-based and hybrid seafood (abroad first); Vietnamese surimi and fish-ball makers testing blends (see line L4); pangasius and tilapia farms and processors, which gain off-flavour benchmarks for their own exports
partners: Can Tho University (fish quality); Nha Trang University (seafood science); Industrial University of Ho Chi Minh City (sensory); an international flavour-chemistry group as co-applicant; Coefficient Giving as funder
capital_note: Tens to hundreds of thousands of USD; Coefficient Giving offered USD 0.1 to 1 million per award in round 1 and USD 1 to 5 million in round 2 (2026)
source_ids: CGG-03; CAP-57; AFN-01; CGG-15; CGG-16; MAC-01
